title: feat: initial opendesk Cloudron package with SSO, mail, store metadata and catalog workflow
body:
## Summary

Initial Cloudron package for [opendesk](https://github.com/useopendesk/opendesk) (Apache-2.0), built from source at upstream commit `898e5943a232b72331daeef76678bf9093b9a210`.

- **Cloudron SSO** (`oidc` addon). First sign-in creates the account; password signup stays closed.
- **Platform mail** through the Cloudron relay (`sendmail` addon).
- **Support mailboxes on Cloudron Mail**: the IMAP/SMTP settings fill themselves in, connections use the internal route, and TLS is still verified. In the mailbox dialog, *Email password* is marked **Recommended**. Forwarding is hidden because the package has no inbound SMTP route.
- PostgreSQL addon (`citext`, `vector`), with data in `/app/data`. The realtime gateway runs under supervisord behind nginx.
- Upstream patches live in `patches/0001`–`0004`. Build images are pinned by digest.
- Community-store metadata: icon, five 3:1 store slides made from upstream screenshots (provenance in `DESIGN.md`), and a Cloudron-format `CHANGELOG`.
- A catalog publish workflow that only runs when `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true` (GHCR image, keyless provenance, `CloudronVersions.json` via the pinned Cloudron CLI 8.2.6), plus a GitHub release workflow.
- Docs: `README.md` (install/setup/config/limits/troubleshooting), `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`, `docs/PUBLISHING.md`, and a draft forum post in `docs/ANNOUNCEMENT.md`.

## Merge method

**Use a merge commit, not squash.** `iconUrl` and `mediaLinks` in `CloudronManifest.json` point at commits `f6e44e2` and `98b89d4`, and those commits must stay reachable from `main`.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`: passed.
- `shellcheck` on `start.sh`, `scripts/*.sh`, `bin/run-realtime`, `bin/opendesk-cli`, `test/package-test.sh`: clean.
- In a scratch copy, `cloudron versions add --state testing` followed by `cloudron versions verify` (CLI 8.2.6): passed.
- Live install updated from this branch with `cloudron update`. `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/admin/` returned 200, and `/v1/auth/config` reports the Cloudron OIDC provider with `signup_enabled:false`.

## Not yet verified

- Cloudron user sign-in and workspace creation; mailbox receive/reply/alias; backup and restore.
- Catalog install. Publishing needs the repository to be public, plus `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` and `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`. Merging does not publish anything.

title: GH#7: update opendesk to bb2b56b
body:
## Summary

Prepare unreleased package 0.1.2 at the exact upstream revision requested by #7,
`bb2b56b5cd6df6c501d04d3efaa61519d6cf3237`, rather than chasing newer main.
Synchronize the Dockerfile, manifest upstream version and license source, and both
changelogs. Preserve all image pins, addons, runtime settings and Cloudron patches.
Leave the generated catalog unchanged.

## Publication boundary — merge hold

**Do not merge without resolving the publication boundary.** The repository's
`CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED` variable is `true`. In
`.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml`, a push to main with an unpublished
manifest version automatically builds and pushes the image, writes the catalog,
tags, and creates a release. Issue #7 explicitly forbids publication without
separate operator authorization. `hold-for-review` prevents an automatic merge
from implicitly publishing 0.1.2. No workflow or repository variable is changed.

## Files Changed

- `Dockerfile`: immutable upstream source pin only.
- `CloudronManifest.json`: package 0.1.2, upstream version and matching license URL.
- `CHANGELOG` and `CHANGELOG.md`: matching unreleased package notes.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: medium; package integration and version metadata, no patch changes.
- Verified source head: `65217f905a53a3e54017ab3775598ada56de54b5`.
- `bash test/package-test.sh`: passed.
- ShellCheck of startup, wrappers, all existing scripts and package test: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Docker source-stage build at the requested SHA: passed; all four Cloudron patches
  apply, including the mailbox-detail hunks at their new offsets.
- Initial full local Docker build: passed; packaged binary reports
  `cloudron-bb2b56b5cd6df6c501d04d3efaa61519d6cf3237` and the same commit.
- `docker build --platform=linux/amd64 --progress=plain --tag cloudron-opendesk-issue7:amd64 .`:
  passed, producing local image
  `sha256:71ebe07ef55acbbd41829bad8fac6a07c51b750e1d625a62846d546ab6018cae`.
  The first emulated amd64 attempt hit a Go compiler deadlock in `html2text`;
  an unchanged retry passed. No source workaround was added.
- Container runtime smoke: `/app/code/opendesk version` reports the exact requested
  commit. `file` confirms both the Go binary and bundled Erlang `beam.smp` are
  x86-64. Frontend TypeScript checks, web/widget/admin builds, static Go build,
  and Elixir production release all completed in the amd64 build.
- `cloudron-package-helper.sh preflight-release v0.1.2`: passed. It warns that
  registry verification of the unchanged `golang:1.27` digest could not complete;
  Docker successfully resolves and uses that digest in the source-stage build.
- No Cloudron deployment, live SSO/mail flow, backup/restore or database upgrade
  qualification is claimed. No image was pushed and no tag, release or catalog
  entry was created.

## Pre-existing dependency advisories (not repaired in this task)

The realtime build resolver flags Bandit 1.12.5 for CVE-2026-105659 (high,
HTTP/2 blocked-send deadlines) and CVE-2026-105660 (medium, request-target
authority). These are not introduced by this update: GitHub returns identical
`realtime/mix.lock` blob SHA `aea1f17acc8a1c7bcc04aa184d109c17fb8e99b4`
for both `898e5943a232b72331daeef76678bf9093b9a210` and the new pin.
Upstream dependency remediation is separate work; the lockfile is not patched here.

## Acceptance review (self-review)

- Direct closeout review found no introduced package-source defect. Evidence
  bundle SHA-256: `51a4e85adf645750c52a7d3a2d1bf78d195396f41a1ad56706a1e2ad24e3fc60`;
  prompt-injection scan: clean.
- Finding verified: default main still pins `898e594`; no duplicate update PR or
  salvageable pushed issue branch existed. Upstream comparison contains four
  commits through the requested revision.
- Packaging guidance retained: reviewed Cloudron base 6.0.0 digest, minimum
  Cloudron 9.1, immutable upstream pin, frozen pnpm lockfiles and existing patches.
- Dependency/runtime declarations checked: Go 1.27.1 and pnpm 12.10.1; existing
  build stages select Go 1.27 and Node 24 without changing upstream lockfiles.
- Required release preflight ran successfully; no tag is proposed by this PR.
- No-publication boundary preserved by keeping the PR held rather than merging
  into the enabled publication workflow.

Resolves #7

Upstream's self-host installer/update timer is not packaged. Upstream's release
checker requires a `vX.Y.Z` binary version; the existing `cloudron-<commit>` build

title: GH#15: chore: release 0.1.3 with the IMAP sync fix
body:
## Summary

Release package 0.1.3 so catalog installs get upstream's fix for IMAP mailboxes that stop syncing after their first pass (forum report: https://forum.cloudron.io/post/131294).

- `CloudronManifest.json`: `version` 0.1.2 → 0.1.3 (the `f9471ba` pin and patches already landed in #14).
- `CHANGELOG` / `CHANGELOG.md`: finalise 0.1.3, leading with the fix; drop the "not authorized" note now that release is authorized.
- `docs/PUBLISHING.md`: qualification step that checks a mailbox keeps receiving after its first sync — the gap that let this ship.

## Root cause

In `bb2b56b` (0.1.2), `syncInsertOpts()` in `internal/email/api_mailboxes.go` used `UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}` with River's default unique states, which include `completed`. A finished `email.sync_mailbox` job blocked every later one-minute `email.sync_due` insert until River pruned it (~24 h). Upstream `9c7cc1a` (#52, included in `f9471ba`) excludes `completed` and adds `ByQueue` so legacy completed rows stop matching immediately on upgrade.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh` passed; shellcheck clean; patches 0001–0004 apply to `f9471ba`.
- Upgrade qualification on a test install (0.1.2 from catalog → this branch built on the server), with a probe IMAP mailbox whose host never resolves: results in the comment below.

Merge with a merge commit (pinned media URLs). Merging publishes via `cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` (`CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`); release is authorized.

Resolves #15

title: GH#12: feat: help centers on custom domains and wildcard subdomains (0.2.0)
body:
## Summary

Help centers on their own domains through Cloudron alias domains, released as package 0.2.0.

- **`CloudronManifest.json`:** `multiDomain: true` lets operators add aliases in the app's *Location*. Version bumped from 0.1.3 to 0.2.0. opendesk stays at `f9471ba`.
- **Exact alias** (for example `help.example.com`): serves the custom domain a brand connects under *Help center → Custom domain*. No package setting is needed. opendesk's DNS check accepts Cloudron's record for the alias, so only the `_opendesk-verify` TXT record is added by hand.
- **Wildcard alias** (for example `*.help.example.com`): `start.sh` sets opendesk's `HELP_DOMAIN` from the only wildcard entry in `CLOUDRON_ALIAS_DOMAINS`, so every brand gets `<slug>.help.example.com`. `HELP_DOMAIN` is now package-owned, so it never names a host Cloudron does not route. It stays unset when there is no wildcard alias, more than one, or a name opendesk would reject. The start log reports which mode is active.
- **Mail is unaffected.** Aliases carry web traffic only. The README says a brand's mailbox usually stays on the main domain, and a domain only needs email enabled in Cloudron for mail addresses on the subdomain itself.
- **Docs:** a README *Help center addresses* section (setup and removal order, DNS records, troubleshooting), `DESCRIPTION.md`, `env.template`, `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`, and a `docs/PUBLISHING.md` qualification step.

## Fixed along the way: `/help/<slug>` never rendered

`nginx.conf` set `proxy_set_header Connection ""` inside `location /`. nginx then drops every `proxy_set_header` inherited from `server` level, so opendesk received `Host: opendesk` (the upstream name). `helpsite.Middleware` matched no host, and every `/help/<slug>` request in 0.1.x served the web app instead of the help center. All proxy headers now live at server level, and one `map` handles `Connection` for both WebSocket upgrades and keepalive. `test/package-test.sh` now rejects any `proxy_set_header` inside a `location`; it flags all five lines of the old config. Client IPs were not affected: opendesk runs with `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1` and reads Cloudron's `X-Forwarded-For`.

## Verification

Disposable install `opendesk-gh12` on a Cloudflare-DNS domain, with an exact alias and a wildcard alias, plus a seeded workspace with brands `acme` and `beta`. All requests below went through Cloudron's public proxy.

title: GH#25: fix: send platform email over STARTTLS to the mail FQDN (0.2.2)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #25. Package **0.2.2** fixes platform email (invitations, sign-in links, password resets, notifications), which times out in 0.2.1.

With `sendmail.requiresValidCertificate`, Cloudron sets `CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTP_SERVER` to the mail FQDN and maps it in `/etc/hosts` to the Docker host (`172.18.0.1`). The host DNATs only the STARTTLS relay port (2587) there. 0.2.1 used the SMTPS port 2465, which exists only on the `mail` container, so every connection timed out.

- `start.sh`: send to the FQDN on `CLOUDRON_MAIL_STARTTLS_PORT` with `SMTP_TLS=starttls`. Without a STARTTLS port, log a warning and keep the log driver. The app no longer stops at startup and never falls back to cleartext.
- `test/package-test.sh`: assert the STARTTLS port and mode, and reject the plain and SMTPS relay variables.
- `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`, `CHANGELOG`, `CHANGELOG.md`, manifest version 0.2.2. The upstream pin is unchanged (`809b80d`).

Upstream reference: `internal/mailer/mailer.go` at 809b80d uses `smtp.DialStartTLS(addr, &tls.Config{ServerName: host, MinVersion: TLS1.2})` for `starttls`. `internal/config/config.go` only refuses `SMTP_TLS=none` with credentials in production. Authentication and hostname verification stay enabled.

## Runtime Testing

**Risk: medium (transport change). Testing: runtime-verified against production's mail path, before and after deploy.**

Production app container (Cloudron 10.1.5, package 0.2.1):

- `/etc/hosts`: `172.18.0.1 mail.marcusquinn.com`
- TCP: `172.18.0.1:2465` timed out (0.2.1's target), `mail:2465` open, `172.18.0.1:465` open.
- Host NAT: `-A DOCKER -d 172.18.0.1/32 -p tcp --dport 2587 -j DNAT --to-destination <mail>:2587`. There is no 2465 equivalent.
- `curl --ssl-reqd smtp://mail.marcusquinn.com:2587`: `STARTTLS`, TLS 1.3, `subject: CN=*.marcusquinn.com`, Let's Encrypt issuer verified, then `250 AUTH LOGIN PLAIN`.
- `bash test/package-test.sh`, ShellCheck on all package scripts, `git diff --check`: pass.

Post-deploy delivery evidence will be added to #25 after the catalog update.
